rows.gap: The criterion has two clauses and they are not in the same state. The named parallel renderers ARE gone and the whole tree is grep-gated for their return, so that clause is met and its proofs stand. 'EXACTLY ONE implementation per interaction' is not met: two of the four interaction kinds have NO implementation of their own and are dispatched to the S1 shell, which draws a line of text and calls itself not-yet-drawn. The gate that reported this row green counted one component serving two kinds as one-per-interaction, so it could only ever see duplicates, never absences. It now checks both directions and its done-check names the two undrawn kinds; this row is honest about the half that is open until they are drawn. The gate's ORDINARY run is now the done-check: the lenient read needs a flag, so "this gate fails while a kind is a placeholder" is true of the run anybody actually makes.

rows.priorNote: SATISFIED under owner ruling entry 334 answer 3 — and the FENCE FINDING that made the ruling necessary is kept here, because it is the reason the criterion could not be met as written. THE FENCE: `assertScriptedProviderNotProduction` (packages/llm/src/scripted-test-provider.ts) throws unless CINATRA_RUNTIME_MODE === 'development' AND NODE_ENV !== 'production'; `lifecycleSeedEnvVerdict` FENCE 1a (src/lib/test-support/lifecycle-seed-fence.ts) answers 404 production-build on NODE_ENV === 'production' before it reads any other gate. `next start` sets NODE_ENV=production and Next inlines that value into the server bundle at build time, so a production-equivalent build and an LLM-backed dispatch are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE by construction. Both fences are shipped product safety, not test scaffolding, and this lane weakened neither. WHAT IS PROVEN. Structural conformance, bidirectionally, against the pinned S0 spec commit (design@6c20871b4108176c1d0193f19ecd2947f6c6355f specs/app-lifecycle-cards.html): every spec anchor is rendered, and every anchor the route renders is in the spec's closed set. PRODUCTION-BUILD cells, on a real `pnpm build` + `next start` (evidence/2573-s7-conformance): the review card PENDING on the page gate region with its island iframe, sandbox tokens and server-minted ref; the island rendering the BUILD-MAP renderer class server-side; and the island's ONE empty document for a ref that does not decode. DEV-RUNTIME cells, each labeled (evidence/2573-s7-visuals-lane): the review card on the chat_thread surface PENDING (C1) and DECIDED (C2), and the recommendation hold on the run_card surface HELD (A1) and decided exactly once (A2). Every row photographed there was written by the shipped writers and read back from cinatra.artifact_review_audit; the only stand-in anywhere is the model layer, and the one DB-level fixture (a single agent_assigned_skills row, in the shape the shipped store writes) is stated on the cell. THE ONE OPEN CELL, recorded rather than rounded up: `C3__review-card__run_card__live-run` is NOT delivered. The run_card host IS declared and a real review gate IS bound to the run — its own step rail draws 'Review changes_requested' and 'Core analysis drifted' — but AgenticRunPanel gates the run_card ReviewGateCard on `isPendingApproval && effectiveHitlContext?.xRenderer === ARTIFACT_REVIEW_REDIRECT_RENDERER_ID && reviewGateCardRef`, and that interrupt context is LIVE ORCHESTRATION STATE rather than a row: it needs a run that actually pauses at the artifact-review checkpoint, i.e. a real LLM-backed execution, and no model credential may reach the capture host. The card suite proves the same component draws on that host ('draws the SAME card on every first-party host, differing only in the frame'); what is missing is the photograph of it under a live pause.

specCommitDrift.why: design#134. The pin above moved to the drawing that gives the run-progress card, in the slot the review card will fill, an explicit reading for the time before the run's output exists, and withdraws the prompt window from every reading inside a conversation. At the previous pin §II's requesting-changes example carried a “Prompt window · this run” panel with its own Send button standing in the assistant's turn, above the thread's own composer — two places to type in one conversation — and the slot the review card fills had no reading at all for the time before it exists. At this pin the slot is read twice, in order: the run-progress placeholder (the card frame with a spinning icon, naming no status and reporting no result) that is replaced, in place and on its own, by the review card once the run's output is generated; and a change request is typed into the thread's own composer at the foot, the only place to type in a conversation. The pin is an IMMUTABLE commit, never a moving head: a pin that follows the head proves nothing, because the document can change under a green claim.
specCommitDrift.differs: Against the previous pin, §II gains the example `run-progress-placeholder-in-thread` — one slot, two readings: the run-progress card (frame, header, spinning icon, nothing to press) then the review card already drawn there — and loses the example `review-prompt-window-in-thread`: the “Prompt window · this run” panel and its Send button are struck from the thread, and typing a change request is now drawn into the thread's own composer at the foot of the column instead. Every remaining prose mention of “the prompt window” inside this spec is restated — the disabled-floor example and the restricted-access example both now read “the chat box” rather than “the prompt window” — and the composer-binding callout in §II states outright that no prompt window is drawn inside a conversation, because the prompt window is the box outside the chat.
